label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.9 a.1 co: Whatever is changed in any way is in some way in…
locator: I q.9 a.1 co.: Omne autem quod quocumque modo mutatur, est aliquo modo in potentia
interpretation: The first proof of God's immutability rests on the general principle that whatever is changed in any way is in some way in potency. Formalized only for succession: a living thing whose life-state differs between two times at which it lives is changed quocumque modo (q.10 a.1 co.: in every motion there is succession). 'Aliquo modo in potentia' is read as potency in the subject (the InPotency of PureAct), the sense q.9 a.1's own conclusion uses for God; q.9 a.2's mutability through a power in another is excluded (DISAMB-POTENCY-IN-SUBJECT-VS-IN-ANOTHER). Beginning or ceasing to live is not claimed under this principle, since Aquinas denies that creation is a change properly speaking; that coverage is the separate unattributed premise STMT-LIFE-BOUNDARY-REQUIRES-POTENCY.
